day.daily_goal: Present your Week 1 clone, then choose and scope the improvement you will build this week.

tasks.intro: Quick stand-up before we get into it.
questions: How are you doing today? Rate your mood from 1-10.
What did you accomplish since the last session?
What do you hope to accomplish today?
Any blockers?
tasks.task_description: Quick daily check-in on mood, progress, and blockers.

tasks.intro: Your Week 1 feedback report is ready. Head to the Performance tab and read the whole thing before answering the questions below.
questions: What feedback resonated as true about how you showed up last week?
Based on your report, what is one specific thing you want to do differently this week?
tasks.task_description: AI-generated report on strengths and growth areas from the past week.

tasks.intro: Each pair presents their clone to the full L2 cohort: what you built, why you chose it, a live demo, and one thing you would improve. Audience — give real attention, you will be asked what stood out.
questions: How did your presentation go — what landed and what felt unclear?
Which presentation from the room stood out to you?
tasks.task_description: Each pair presents their clone to the full L2 cohort.

tasks.intro: Take a real break. This afternoon is about picking your next challenge.

tasks.v2_learning_goal: Builder can describe RICE, MoSCoW, and the Impact/Effort matrix, explain what each one optimizes for, and identify which context each is best suited to.
tasks.v2_lesson_content: RICE scores Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort: (Reach × Impact × Confidence) / Effort. MoSCoW sorts Must, Should, Could, and Won’t have this time. The Impact/Effort matrix compares expected impact and required effort. No framework replaces judgment.
tasks.intro: Most feature ideas are not worth building — the skill is knowing which ones are.
tasks.task_description: RICE, MoSCoW, and the Impact/Effort matrix — three frameworks for deciding what to build next.

tasks.intro: Now that you have learned about feature prioritization frameworks, take a few minutes to discuss as a table. Which framework do you think gets skipped most often by teams, and why?
tasks.task_description: Table teachback and discussion on feature prioritization frameworks.

tasks.intro: Using the feedback you got in this morning’s presentations and the frameworks from the teachback, brainstorm 3-5 possible improvements to your own clone with your pair, then pick your top one.
questions: What is on your wishlist?
Which one are you choosing, and why?
tasks.task_description: Brainstorm possible improvements using peer feedback and prioritization frameworks, then pick one.

tasks.intro: Open the Pursuit PRD Template and use the New Feature section. Document the Current User Journey step by step, marking where it breaks down. Fill it in with your pair.
questions: When done, submit your PRD Google Doc link using the assignment button.
tasks.task_title: Create Your Feature PRD & Submit to Pathfinder
tasks.task_description: Draft the improvement PRD using the New Feature template.

tasks.intro: Day 5 done. A lot happened — presentations, prioritization, and a new PRD. Take a few minutes to reflect.
questions: Why is your chosen improvement the right one to build this week?
tasks.task_description: End-of-day reflection on what was built and learned.
tasks.conclusion: Tomorrow morning is your Cycle 1 baseline assessment, then you are diagramming how the internet actually works. Come ready to focus.
